project.name: club-events
project.summary: Members see upcoming club events and sign up; the organiser sees who is coming.

structure.public/: what runs in the browser: pages and their scripts, no business rules
structure.server.js: HTTP only: routes, input parsing, status codes; calls src/, never touches files
structure.src/events.js: business rules: listing, sign-up rules, attendee list
structure.src/store.js: the only code that reads or writes the data file; every change goes through update()
structure.test/: one test file per part; API tests start the real server

features.name: See upcoming events
features.user_action: Opens the site and sees upcoming events with date, place and free places.

flow.does: Home page with the list of events
Server sends the home page and its script
Server sends the page script
Loads events from the API and shows them
GET /api/events
Upcoming events only, with places left
Reads events and sign-ups from data/db.json

tests.find: lists only upcoming events, soonest first, with places left
pages are served and unknown paths are 404

untested: How the list looks and behaves in a real browser (public/app.js has no automated test)

decisions.decision: One JSON file instead of a database
decisions.why: a club has tens of events; nothing to install or run

features.name: Sign up for an event
features.user_action: Types name and email under an event and presses Sign up; sees a confirmation with a cancel code, or why it failed (full, already signed up).

flow.does: Sign-up form under each event
Sends the form and shows the result
POST /api/events/:id/signups
Checks email, capacity and duplicates
Adds the sign-up to data/db.json through the write queue

tests.find: sign-up is saved and reduces places left
sign-up rejects bad input, duplicates, unknown and full events
POST /api/events/:id/signups signs up and reports errors as JSON
sign-ups and cancellations at the same moment do not undo each other

untested: The form in a real browser (messages, refresh after sign-up)

decisions.why: so Sam@x.org and sam@x.org count as the same person for duplicates

decisions.decision: All sign-up rules live in src/events.js, not in the page
decisions.why: the browser can be bypassed; the server must decide

decisions.decision: Each sign-up gets a random 8-character cancel code, shown once
decisions.why: needed by "Cancel a sign-up" so that only the person who signed up can cancel

decisions.decision: All writes go through store.update (one at a time); save is no longer public
decisions.why: simultaneous sign-ups were being lost; nothing can bypass the queue now

debt.text: store.save rewrites the whole file after a separate store.load. Two sign-ups at the same moment can overwrite each other (the last write wins). Accepted for launch: a small club rarely has simultaneous sign-ups. Fixed: all writes go through store.update, which runs them one at a time.
The write queue only protects one server process. Running several processes on the same data file would bring the problem back; that would need a database or a file lock.

features.name: Organiser sees who is coming
features.user_action: The organiser opens the organiser page, enters the organiser key and sees each event's attendees.

flow.does: Organiser page
Server sends the organiser page and its script
Server sends the organiser script
Asks the API with the key, shows the list
GET /api/events/:id/signups, only with the organiser key
Attendee list for one event
Reads sign-ups

untested: The organiser page in a real browser
What happens when ORGANISER_KEY is not set in production (returns 503; not exercised by a test)

decisions.decision: A shared organiser key in an environment variable, not accounts
decisions.why: one organiser; accounts would be most of the work

features.name: Email reminder the day before
features.user_action: Each person signed up gets an email the day before the event.

flow.does: Finds tomorrow's events and their attendees
Sends the email (provider not chosen yet)

features.name: Cancel a sign-up
features.user_action: Enters the event, their email and the cancel code shown when they signed up, and presses Cancel; the place becomes free again.

flow.does: Cancel form on the home page
Sends event, email and code
POST /api/events/:id/cancellations
Removes the sign-up only if email and code match
Removes the sign-up from data/db.json through the write queue

tests.find: cancel with the right email and code frees the place
POST /api/events/:id/cancellations cancels with the code from sign-up
sign-ups and cancellations at the same moment do not undo each other

untested: The cancel form in a real browser
Someone who lost their code has no way to cancel (by design for now)

decisions.decision: Cancelling needs a secret code given at sign-up
decisions.why: with email alone, anyone could cancel someone else's place
